sourceMathEvidence: The question says the polynomial product plus k is the perfect square of some quadratic f(x) and asks for k+f(5), without fixing the sign of f.
solutionMathEvidence: Factoring and pairing gives (x−1)(x−4)(x−2)(x−3)+k=(t+4)(t+6)+k for t=x²−5x. The square condition fixes k=1 and the polynomial as (t+5)², but the supplied solution chooses f=t+5 without justifying its sign.
ambiguityWitness: Both f₊(x)=x²−5x+5 and f₋(x)=−(x²−5x+5) are quadratic and have the same square. They give f₊(5)=5 and f₋(5)=−5, so k+f(5) is 6 or −4.
